turns.speaker: Steve
turns.text: Inversion of meaning can indeed be fascinating. Take for example the phrase "mishka" in Russia, which literally means "bad luck," but is often used to ward off misfortune. In the West, "good luck" is more commonly used. In some cultures, like Japan, "honne" (outside self) and "tatemae" (inside self) exist, where the "bad" or "good" truth is often hidden beneath a social facade.
